coverage_scope: Curated partial index of the load-bearing backbone: the frontier reduction, the master theorem schema, finite certificates, arbitrary-order structural theorems, and selected on-disk H31/H22 component-level claim documents. This is NOT a complete mapping of every claim, proof obligation, boundary/divisor certificate, evidence carrier, or relationship in the repository. A backing document exists for every entry; primary and audit carriers are mapped when present or their absence/indexing state is recorded.

conventions.status_field_semantics: legacy composite summary of mathematical state, scope, evidence assessment, and lifecycle at this entry's granularity; it is not a single proof-strength ladder and must be read with the owning document

status_semantics.verified: an exact mathematical claim is accepted at the entry's stated scope; the evidence carrier may be a mapped script, an in-document proof, or an explicitly recorded certificate chain; independent audit and formalization are separate
status_semantics.verified_finite: an exact finite claim is accepted through the recorded finite certificate or exhaustive computation and its stated bridge; it says nothing beyond that finite scope
status_semantics.verified_generic: an exact claim is accepted over the stated component function field or generic point only; excluded divisors, special fibres, and projective boundaries remain separate obligations unless explicitly closed
status_semantics.partial: one or more exact subclaims are accepted, but the stated parent obligation or case cover remains incomplete
status_semantics.candidate: a proposed claim or route has not passed the review needed to become a live accepted result
status_semantics.exploratory: the entry records reconnaissance, search, translation, or a research programme and is not a proof-active conclusion
status_semantics.withdrawn: the formerly claimed conclusion or route is explicitly non-live and cannot be used as a mathematical premise; preserved identities or diagnostics retain only their stated narrower scope
status_semantics.partially_withdrawn: a specified part of the earlier claim or route is non-live while separately identified surviving subclaims retain their stated status
status_semantics.superseded: a later artifact replaces this one for live use; this entry remains only for lineage unless an explicit surviving subclaim is identified
status_semantics.framework: an organizational theorem schema or proof architecture, not a claim that all named obligations are closed
status_semantics.open: the target claim is unresolved at the entry's stated scope

conventions.axis_separation: scope, evidence mode, independent-audit status, formalization status, lifecycle, and execution outcome are independent; proved, verified, experimental, failed, timeout, and inconclusive are defined in the contract document and must not be collapsed into one ladder

audit_provenance_semantics.independent_modular_audit: legacy broad mapping label: a distinct audit script exists; the literal method and independence scope must be read from that audit and may be exact-rational or share construction machinery
audit_provenance_semantics.independent_exact_identity_audit: a distinct exact audit rederives the specifically named identities and does not assert a broader theorem conclusion
audit_provenance_semantics.none_exists: no carrier exists for this field and exact claim at this entry's granularity; this is an explicit absence, not an unmapped gap
audit_provenance_semantics.not_yet_mapped: a carrier may exist for this field but has not been entered into this ledger
audit_provenance_semantics.historical_certificate_chain: the audit is the SAT/DRAT replay chain, not one script

dependencies.policy: every current entry must retain an empty array; do not infer independence or absence of mathematical premises; typed mathematical, executable, provenance, audit, corroboration, and historical relationships belong in a separately reviewed proof-obligation graph

conventions.assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: non-exhaustive compact scope summary for navigation; the owning mathematical document controls and must be reviewed before the entry is used
conventions.primary_verifier: mapped primary evidence carrier when one is recorded; it is an evidence relationship, not a mathematical dependency
conventions.independent_audit: mapped audit carrier when one is recorded; independence is scoped to the recorded method and shared machinery must still be disclosed
conventions.policy: modular evidence, numerical experiments, timeouts, and failed solver runs are never proofs; they are corroboration or diagnostics only
conventions.document_sha256_16: first 16 hex chars of the SHA-256 of the committed git blob (git show :path), not the working-tree bytes; identical on every platform because the index stores LF. check_hygiene.py recomputes and compares every non-null value.
conventions.claim_package: the claim package root directory, e.g. claims/p5/h22/disjoint-mixed-star
conventions.proof_variant: canonical | alternate | null — which independent proof of the same claim this entry documents
conventions.subpackage: null | alternate | boundaries — subdirectory of the claim package holding the entry's files

assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: the theorem classifies exactly the fixed complete eight-vertex U7D endpoint-label support and does not classify arbitrary matrix-unit label supports or arbitrary order
the complete same-multidegree block consists of all 70 words with colour counts (4,4,0); empty fibres are retained as tautological zero equations
the exact fibre census has 57 empty, 10 singleton, and 3 binomial fibres, with the binomials exactly the imported active cycle
all 28 physical amplitudes are inverted in the complete nonzero r=1 Laurent torus; before saturation a singleton equation forces a zero physical amplitude and leaves this support stratum
the saturated ideal and its elimination in Q[H] are the unit ideal, which is fixed-support exclusion rather than a stronger compatible holonomy polynomial
the other two balanced binary blocks of the unpermuted table are empty; global colour relabelling transports the active-block census but is not a symmetry claim about the unpermuted table

same multidegree is only a grading under current theorems; a universal complete-block unit-or-syzygy lemma, aggregate holonomy, cross-multiplicity coupling, pure cofactor exits, the deeper branch, r=1 exclusion, and the global conjecture remain open
entries.note: For the fixed complete U7D endpoint-label table, the full 70-word (4,4,0) block has 57 empty, 10 singleton, and exactly three binomial fibres. Any singleton target equation is a unit after Laurent localization at all physical amplitudes, so the complete same-degree ideal and its intersection with Q[H] are both (1). This excludes the fixed support in the active cycle's own multidegree but yields no stronger compatible holonomy polynomial and no arbitrary-order exclusion. Independent matching-first and word-first exact checkers verify the census, distinct singleton unit certificates, the cycle regression, and all six global colour relabellings. Global Krenn-Gu remains UNRESOLVED.

entries.name: Matrix-Unit Complete Same-Multidegree Fibre-Lattice Reduction and Binomial Parity Dichotomy Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: exact matching-monomial and group-algebra arguments over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field at every even order
the word multidegree is mixed, so every word in the complete block is a target-zero coordinate; empty matching fibres are retained as tautologies
the physical stratum is the complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit Laurent torus with one fixed ordered endpoint-label pair and one invertible amplitude per edge
normalization uses every compatible matching in every word fibre and divides only by an invertible reference matching monomial
the within-fibre difference lattice may be nonsaturated; freeness over its group algebra uses coset representatives and does not assume a unimodular pivot or direct-summand lattice
the signed integer-kernel parity criterion is imported from the earlier integer signed-lattice transport theorem; the new content is the complete-block descent and exact holonomy-elimination bridge
a parity-consistent all-binomial block is proper and imposes exactly H=(-1)^m on a selected active cycle, but an actual full physical-torus point is asserted only over C
the theorem does not force a singleton or odd dependency and does not classify aggregate fibres, other multidegrees, pure-cofactor exits, deeper blockers, the r=1 branch, or the global conjecture
entries.note: For any complete mixed same-multidegree target block on the complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit torus, dividing each nonempty fibre by one reference matching descends the exact ideal to the group algebra of all within-fibre matching differences. The ambient Laurent ring is free over that group algebra, so unit status and any in-lattice holonomy elimination descend faithfully even for nonsaturated lattices. A singleton is a unit. If all nonempty fibres are binomial, an odd signed integer-kernel dependency is exactly the unit branch; otherwise the block is proper and a selected m-cycle eliminates to precisely (H-(-1)^m), with no stronger same-degree holonomy polynomial. Aggregate fibres remain open. Independent matching-first/Smith-form and no-import word-first/unimodular-kernel checkers audit the bridge. Global Krenn-Gu remains UNRESOLVED.

entries.name: Matrix-Unit Binomial-Core Torsion-Sheet and Rank-One Aggregate Quotient Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: exact finitely generated abelian group-algebra, Smith torsion, finite Fourier, and Laurent PID arguments over C at every even order
the input is the proved U7E normalization of one complete mixed same-multidegree target block on the complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit torus
one selected active transport cycle has complete binomial fibres and every one of its cycle equations belongs to the chosen binomial core
the selected signed binomial core is parity-consistent; an odd dependency is already the U7E unit branch
extension of the core sign character uses divisibility of C*; changing the extension changes only the quotient presentation by a character automorphism
nonsaturation is retained as Smith torsion and every torsion character sheet is required for a unit-ideal conclusion
quotient free rank zero is completely decided by finite character evaluations and free rank one by exact univariate Laurent gcds after removing monomial units
an aggregate equation can only toggle the selected cycle elimination between (1) and (H-(-1)^m); this conclusion does not apply to an aggregate cycle fibre
the theorem does not force a fully binomial cycle, quotient free rank at most one, death of every low-rank sheet, or a uniform rank-at-least-two unit certificate
aggregate cycle fibres, cross-multiplicity coupling, pure/deeper exits, the general r=1 exclusion, and the global conjecture remain open
entries.note: For a parity-consistent binomial core containing every fibre of an active binomial cycle, a character automorphism untwists the core and identifies its exact residual algebra with C[L/L_B]. Smith torsion gives a finite product of Laurent character sheets. Residual aggregate unit/properness is completely decided by scalar evaluations in quotient free rank zero and by exact univariate Laurent gcds in free rank one. Killing every sheet makes the block a unit; any surviving sheet leaves exactly H=(-1)^m, so aggregate equations cannot produce a different stronger nonunit holonomy polynomial. Aggregate cycle fibres and free rank at least two remain open. Independent SymPy/Smith/Fourier and no-import Gaussian/Euclidean implementations audit the mechanisms. Global Krenn-Gu remains UNRESOLVED.

entries.name: Matrix-Unit Cross-Multiplicity Global Target-Lattice and Holonomy Dichotomy Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: exact finitely generated group-algebra and matching-support arguments over C at every positive even order
the physical stratum is one fixed complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit Laurent torus with one endpoint-label pair and one invertible amplitude per edge
the selected system may contain mixed target-zero equations from arbitrary word multidegrees and any subset of the three pure target equations
each nonzero mixed residual is divided only by an invertible reference matching monomial; empty mixed fibres are tautologies and an empty pure fibre is already a unit certificate
pure target constants are retained as absolute anchor terms and are not silently homogenized into the endpoint-character kernel
the global support-difference lattice may be nonsaturated; freeness uses a full coset basis and does not assume a direct summand
different multidegrees share one exact endpoint-character-kernel algebra after normalization, but common physical variables or nonzero lattice overlap alone do not force a unit ideal
the direct-sum separation theorem is a sufficient no-coupling criterion, not a classification of every possible lattice interaction
the global holonomy dichotomy assumes every complete fibre of the selected active cycle is binomial and belongs to a parity-consistent core; aggregate cycle fibres remain outside it
arbitrary residual target equations can only toggle a fully binomial cycle between the unit ideal and exactly H=(-1)^m; cross-multiplicity unit forcing remains open
the torsion-sheet criteria completely decide quotient free ranks zero and one across multidegrees; free rank at least two remains an exact multivariate Laurent ideal problem
the theorem does not exclude the general r=1 branch, pure-cofactor exits, deeper blockers, or the global conjecture
entries.note: For any selected exact target equations on a fixed complete nonzero matrix-unit support, reference normalization descends the combined ideal faithfully to its global support-difference group algebra. Mixed equations from arbitrary endpoint-colour multidegrees lie in one endpoint-character kernel; pure targets add exact anchor directions. Direct-sum difference lattices provably do not couple despite shared physical variables. Once an active cycle is fully binomial and parity consistent, arbitrary cross-multiplicity and pure residuals either make the combined ideal a unit or leave exactly H=(-1)^m; the rank-zero and rank-one torsion-sheet criteria apply globally. This proves the algebraic interface but not the load-bearing unit-forcing mechanism. Independent imported-fixture/SymPy and no-import bitmask/Fraction audits verify the mechanisms. entries.name: Matrix-Unit Minimal Pure-Cofactor Matching-Covered Core and Single-Cycle Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: exact perfect-matching support, hafnian factorization, and alternating-exchange arguments over a field of characteristic different from two at every even order
the input is a least-cardinality even pure-shore residual whose hafnian vanishes although its support has a perfect matching
the active graph is the first-cofactor graph C_ij=z_ij haf(R-{i,j}), not the full pure support graph
least-cardinality selection is load-bearing when an allowed edge is promoted to a nonzero cofactor and when allowed-core connectedness is proved
the active graph equals the union of all support perfect matchings and is connected and matching-covered with minimum degree at least two
support edges outside the active graph may remain physically present but belong to no perfect matching of the residual and have structurally zero first cofactors
the degree-two branch is one even cycle with exactly two matching monomials, one primitive signed Laurent relation, and unique monomial complements for every cycle edge
the branching branch has at least three perfect matchings, cyclomatic rank at least two, and positive even branching excess
the connected branching exchange core is not claimed to force a deeper blocker, and the primitive cycle relation is not claimed to be inconsistent
pure-cofactor exclusion, aggregate active-cycle fibres, the general r=1 branch, and the global conjecture remain open
entries.note: For a least supported pure hafnian cancellation, the nonzero first-cofactor graph is exactly the allowed-edge graph. Hafnian factorization across its components and least-cardinality selection force one connected matching-covered core. Every active edge lies on an alternating cycle relative to every fixed perfect matching. Degree two is one even cycle with exactly two terms, a primitive signed relation, and monomial first cofactors; otherwise the core has at least three matchings, cyclomatic rank at least two, and either two branch sites or one degree-at-least-four site. Independent tuple-recursive/Fraction and no-import bitmask/incidence audits verify the mechanisms and sharpness boundaries. Global Krenn-Gu remains UNRESOLVED.

entries.name: Matrix-Unit Minimal Pure-Cofactor Port Aggregate and Conformal-Fan Reduction Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: exact perfect-matching and alternating-cycle arguments over a field of characteristic different from two at every even order; sharpness families are over Q
the input is the connected matching-covered active graph of a least-cardinality even supported pure hafnian cancellation from the preceding theorem
perfect matchings are partitioned by the unique incident edge at a chosen root vertex, and the corresponding port sum is the nonzero first cofactor
the sparse case means the total number of residual perfect matchings equals the root degree; then every port is a singleton and each matching differs from the reference on one alternating cycle
the aggregate case concerns a multi-monomial pure first-cofactor port and is not identified with an aggregate active mixed-word fibre
the conformal exchange fan and theta carriers are subgraphs closed under the reference matching; they are not asserted to be induced or mutually disjoint
the two theta profiles count perfect matchings on the displayed theta edge set; extra physical support chords on the same vertices are not removed
the sparse d-fan family, the K4 one-open-port profile, and the K3,3 aggregate profile are exact pure residuals, not complete matrix-unit witnesses
branch degree, conformal-fan topology, and the sparse Laurent sum alone do not force a contradiction or deeper-blocker entry
mixed fan coupling, aggregate-port control, pure-cofactor exclusion, the general r=1 branch, and the global conjecture remain open
entries.note: At every branch vertex of a least supported pure hafnian cancellation, all residual perfect matchings partition into nonzero cofactor ports. If the matching count equals the root degree, every port is a singleton: the matchings are single alternating-cycle flips of a reference, their union is a conformal d-route fan, and the residual gives one exact d-nomial Laurent relation. Otherwise a nonzero aggregate pure-cofactor port is forced. Two exits contain a conformal theta with exactly the all-odd three-matching or odd/even/even two-matching profile. Exact Q families realize sparse fans for every d>=3, both cubic theta profiles, and a genuine aggregate port, so pure fan topology alone cannot close U7. Independent recursive-hafnian and no-import edge-mask/route-state/permutation audits verify the mechanisms. Global Krenn-Gu remains UNRESOLVED.

entries.name: Matrix-Unit Aggregate Active-Cycle Defect Factorisation and Split-Fibre Sharpness Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: the arbitrary-order input is an established active transport cycle in the complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit branch over C, with every compatible matching included in each cycle fibre equation
each aggregate defect is the sum of all extra compatible matching monomials divided only by the selected nonzero outgoing matching monomial
the exact formula H=(-1)^m product_i(1+A_i) uses cyclic reindexing of the selected incoming diagonal matchings and introduces no aggregate-sum denominator
aggregate size does not imply A_i is nonzero; a split aggregate has nonempty extra terms whose normalized sum vanishes
the sharpness family assigns one nonzero matrix unit to all 28 pairs and contains all three endpoint labels at every vertex
the sharpness parameters satisfy t!=0 and 1+2t!=0 so the new edge 47 and selected edge 24 remain nonzero
the complete selected cycle fibres have sizes 5,2,2; the remaining six completion edges are incompatible with all three cycle words
the zero elimination ideal is for the three selected complete cycle equations in Q[x^+-1,t^+-1,H^+-1,(1+2t)^-1], not for the complete GHZ target ideal
all three pure target coefficients of the family are zero, so the family is not a Krenn-Gu witness or an apparent counterexample

entries.note: For an arbitrary active transport cycle, normalizing every extra compatible matching by the selected outgoing matching gives gauge-invariant defects A_i and the exact identity H=(-1)^m product_i(1+A_i). Aggregate extra terms may cancel separately, so a combinatorially aggregate fibre can retain the binomial sign. An exact complete locally concise eight-vertex matrix-unit family has complete cycle-fibre sizes 5,2,2 and H=-2/(1+2t); its selected cycle subsystem has zero elimination ideal in H. At t=1/2 the three extra terms are 1/2,-1,1/2 and split off exactly. The family has zero pure target coefficients and is not a witness. entries.name: Matrix-Unit Aggregate Extra-Matching Target Attachment Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: the arbitrary-order application is inside the complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit branch over C and starts with an imported active transport cycle plus one compatible extra matching whose offdiagonal core is nonempty
a conformally minimal residual R is minimal among zero hafnians whose support on both R and its complement inside the original cancelling shore has a perfect matching

the primitive-cycle, sparse-fan, and aggregate-port relation is embedded termwise by a fixed matching completion; this is an exact branch equation at the hypothetical witness, not a universal target-ideal generator away from the cancellation branch

if all source shore hafnians are nonzero, the imported bridge square/hexagon alternative gives deeper data or a nonzero diagonal matching at another word; the complete target equation is used only after that exact bridge step
the outside-or-parallel conclusion assumes a shortest directed active transport cycle among the available no-deeper noncancelling bridge arcs
the ten-vertex sharpness family is defined over Q(t) with t!=0 and 1+t!=0; it assigns one nonzero matrix unit to all 45 pairs and is locally concise

the family has complete selected fibre sizes 3,2,2, all three pure target coefficients exactly one, and an extra bridge output equal to the selected successor matching, so the new successor-fibre difference is zero

entries.note: For every offdiagonal extra matching in an aggregate active-cycle fibre, a cancelling source or bridge shore contains a conformally minimal connected matching-covered residual whose primitive cycle, sparse fan, or aggregate port embeds termwise in one mixed target fibre with identical exponent differences. Otherwise bridge normalization enters the deeper branch or the complete target equation makes another word active. On a shortest cycle that word is outside or is the selected successor. entries.name: Matrix-Unit Diagonal Aggregate Shore-Product and Primitive-Exchange Sharpness Theorem
assumptions_and_excluded_divisors: the arbitrary-order application is inside the complete nonzero r=1 matrix-unit branch over C and starts with an imported active transport cycle whose extra compatible matchings all have empty offdiagonal core

the diagonal fibre at each active word is the exact Cartesian product of the three pure-shore support-matching sets; the active diagonal coefficient is nonzero, so all three shore hafnians are nonzero
the primitive alternating-cycle conclusion is an incidence-difference support direction obtained by flipping one symmetric-difference component; it is not asserted to be a vanishing binomial relation
the diagonal shore lattices are direct because they have disjoint physical edge-coordinate supports; this does not classify their intersections with target lattices at other words
shortest-cycle minimality supplies no new arc for a diagonal extra, and the bridge/deeper alternative cannot be invoked on its empty offdiagonal core

universal complete-target unit forcing, useful non-direct overlap, proper-subshore cancellation, the deeper-blocker branch, the general r=1 branch, and the global conjecture remain open

Aggregate size forces one primitive one-shore alternating-cycle direction, but not a vanishing binomial, bridge arc, odd dependency, or pure-cofactor zero. The exact cycle equations have a shore-product normal form. A complete locally concise twelve-vertex Q(t) family has the unique shortest active 3/2/2 cycle, one diagonal extra, all pure coefficients one, physical-variable overlap, and a saturated direct rank-four fibre lattice with no integer dependency; its selected holonomy is -1/(1+t) with zero selected-plus-pure elimination. An outside singleton makes the complete target ideal a unit, so the family is not a witness.
